code_review.project_type: web application — React SPA frontend + FastAPI REST backend (AI-patterns showcase gallery)

existing_self_description.text: Built with Spec4 (BWS4) is a living showcase of common AI application patterns, presented as a collection of small, self-contained example apps behind a single landing page. Each example demonstrates one pattern end-to-end: how it's built, what it depends on, and how it behaves, so that visitors unfamiliar with the underlying technique can understand it by seeing it work rather than by reading about it abstractly.

architecture.summary: Monorepo with a layered, feature-module backend: thin FastAPI routers per example app delegate to per-feature service modules, all built on a shared framework-services layer (model registry, generation, agent runtime, embedding, web search, storage) and a SQLAlchemy/Alembic DB layer. The frontend mirrors this with per-app directories lazy-loaded via route-based code-splitting.

change_risks.risk: README explicitly warns the ordered chains of free-tier model slugs rot as providers retire them; both the tool-calling and text-generation chains decay independently
change_risks.mitigation_hint: any phase touching generation should plan for slug refresh and rely on the registry's fallback/bench mechanism rather than hardcoding slugs

change_risks.risk: both lanes read slugs from the same registry and pass through the same usage-limit gate; changes that split those paths would let the lanes disagree about available models or spend unseen budget
change_risks.mitigation_hint: route any new model access through backend/app/services/model_registry.py and the shared usage-limit gate

change_risks.risk: projection is fitted once at startup over the curated preset set and only ever applied afterwards; re-fitting would move existing points and break the example's core demonstration
change_risks.mitigation_hint: never re-fit the projection when adding features; only apply the fitted transform to new texts

change_risks.risk: a chain whose second call failed is deliberately returned as HTTP 200 with status 'critique_failed' so call 1's output survives; converting this to 4xx/5xx would push clients into their error branch and discard the draft
change_risks.mitigation_hint: preserve the 200 + status-field contract in backend/app/api/chained_calls.py when extending the chain

change_risks.risk: per-UTC-day caps are enforced before any provider call; new metered capabilities that bypass the gate could drain the shared free-tier quota of this unauthenticated demo
change_risks.mitigation_hint: route new metered capabilities through the shared usage-limit gate (see migration 0007_usage_limit_daily_window.py and backend/tests/test_usage_windows.py)

security_observations: Application is deliberately unauthenticated; abuse protection is per-UTC-day usage caps enforced before provider calls
CORS allows exactly one origin (the deployed web_client), never '*' (backend/app/main.py)
render.yaml marks secrets sync: false so they are entered in the Render dashboard rather than committed
Custom text submitted to the embeddings placement route is never persisted (backend/app/api/embeddings.py docstring)
other_notes: Monorepo split build systems: backend is uv-managed at repo root (pyproject.toml); frontend is npm + Vite 8 (frontend/package.json) — build/dev/lint/typecheck commands run from frontend/, test and run from repo root
Secondary test command: `npm test` (vitest) in frontend/
Deploy start command (Render): `uv run uvicorn backend.app.main:app --host 0.0...` per render.yaml
Alembic migrations configured via backend/alembic.ini; migration invocation not wrapped in a documented command
Backend declares no linter, formatter, or type checker in pyproject.toml (frontend has oxlint + tsc)
torch is pinned to a CPU-only wheel index via [[tool.uv.index]] pytorch-cpu in pyproject.toml
render.yaml build pre-downloads the ~88 MB sentence-transformers model to avoid cold-start downloads and Hugging Face rate limits
CLAUDE.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, and CLA.md exist but their contents were not shown; they may document additional commands

.env.example exists at repo root; README prerequisites imply a Neon Postgres connection string, OpenRouter API key, and Exa API key are required, but exact variable names were not visible in the evidence
Every source file carries a '# Built with Spec4 AI - https://spec4.ai' header comment
